drafts.title: Front seats: extended thigh support for tall drivers and reliable memory restore
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend the front seat thigh support for noticeably more leg contact and the seat memory reliably restores their saved seating position when they select their profile.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat provides an adjustable thigh-extension of at least 70 mm from the standard cushion edge; seat memory restores the saved driver position within 10 seconds on selection with a success rate ≥98% over 100 consecutive park-start cycles.
assumptions: Measurement follows BMW seat measurement protocol (thigh extension measured from standard cushion edge in the most-forward occupant setting).
Success rate measured across representative temperature range and occupant weights.
No change to requested foam density (SCOPE-E09) is assumed; if foam changes are required this will be evaluated separately.
uncertainties: Packaging space and seat track length available in final vehicle architecture may limit achievable extension.
Trade-offs between extension length and seat heating/ventilation or side bolster geometry.

drafts.title: Cup holders sized for common bottles and secure retention
drafts.description: Cup holders fit the majority of commonly used bottles and travel mugs without adapters and hold them securely to avoid rattle during normal driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept cylindrical drink containers up to 88 mm diameter and retain containers securely (no audible rattle and <10 mm lateral movement) for 95% of a test set of 50 common bottle/mug samples.
assumptions: Test set of 50 bottle/mug samples is representative of frequently used consumer sizes (including common sport bottles and travel mugs).
uncertainties: Some oversized or non-cylindrical novelty containers may still require adapters.
Interior trim variation might affect achievable maximum diameter in specific locations.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on first attempt
drafts.description: When the customer performs the standard hands-free foot gesture, the tailgate opens reliably on the first attempt and does so quickly.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Tailgate opens on the first valid hands-free gesture in ≥95% of trials (n=200) and the median time from valid gesture to tailgate fully open is ≤1.5 seconds in typical parking scenarios.
assumptions: Valid gesture is performed from 0.5–1.5 m behind the vehicle and follows the existing OEM gesture definition.
Tests include common footwear (shoe, boot) and small amounts of mud/snow on shoes to reflect realistic use.
uncertainties: Very heavy ice/snow or large objects obstructing sensor line-of-sight may still require additional attempts.
Interference from aftermarket devices or heavy electromagnetic noise could affect sensor performance.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with broad color and brightness customization
drafts.description: Customers can choose from a broad palette of ambient lighting colors and multiple brightness levels to tailor the interior mood.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 distinct color hues and at least 10 discrete brightness levels (per ambient zone), plus at least 6 preset scenes selectable from the UI.
assumptions: Color selection UI allows per-zone selection and saving to driver profiles.
Color gamut covers commonly perceived distinct hues (visible differences between adjacent presets).
uncertainties: Perceived color differences can vary with cabin materials and lighting; calibration across trims is required.
Power/thermal constraints may limit maximum brightness in certain zones.

drafts.title: Exterior door handles operate reliably after freezing weather
drafts.description: Flush exterior door handles open reliably after freezing conditions so customers are not locked out or required to chip ice away.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles open on the first unlock attempt within 5 seconds after being exposed to -15°C for 2 hours with up to 3 mm surface ice, in ≥95% of test trials (n≥50).
assumptions: Test ice build-up is representative (3 mm distributed surface ice formed under controlled humidity).
Vehicle battery state-of-charge is within normal operating range for cold starts.
uncertainties: Extreme conditions (below -30°C) or very thick ice layers may still impair operation.
Mechanical de-icing solutions may add maintenance complexity or weight.

drafts.title: Rear legroom at least match main competitors in the segment
drafts.description: Rear passengers enjoy rear legroom that is at least as generous as the main competitors in this vehicle segment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear knee clearance (measured per BMW interior benchmark protocol) is ≥920 mm, which meets or exceeds the documented average of the main competitors for this segment.
assumptions: Competitor average rear knee clearance for the segment is assumed to be approximately 920 mm based on current benchmarking data.
Measurements use the same reference points as the competitor benchmark (seat back to knee point method).
uncertainties: Electric vehicle packaging or large battery packs can reduce usable interior length and may require trade-offs.
Final competitor benchmarks may shift by launch; ongoing benchmarking is required.

drafts.title: Trunk includes a user-accessible 12 V power outlet suitable for running a cooler box
drafts.description: Customers can plug a standard 12 V cooler into a trunk-mounted socket to power it during trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A 12 V power socket is installed in the trunk, accessible without tools; it can power a 40 W cooler continuously for at least 3 hours while the vehicle is in accessory mode (verified in a controlled test).
assumptions: Typical portable 12 V coolers draw approximately 40 W.
Accessory mode provides continuous power for at least the test duration without engaging main drivetrain.
uncertainties: Longer run times will be affected by vehicle architecture (battery, accessory mode limits) and may require additional power-management rules.
Local regulations for power delivery in parked vehicles might require design constraints.

drafts.title: Front end to meet new EU pedestrian protection rules (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers request the vehicle front end comply with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested: front-end design that meets the customer ask to comply with the new EU pedestrian protection requirements (subject to certification by authorities).
assumptions: Regulatory interpretation, test procedures and final requirements will be provided by the relevant EU authority prior to certification.
uncertainties: Regulatory details and test dates may change and will affect implementation timelines.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation request — certification and compliance are handled by the regulatory and engineering teams, not a customer-facing product requirement for scope.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the rear seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested: rear-seat airbags meet FMVSS 208 certification as requested by customers.
assumptions: Certification requires engagement with US regulatory authorities and formal test campaigns.
uncertainties: Certification timelines and technical constraints may require design iterations.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation request — certification is out of scope for product-level customer requirements.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern compliant with ECE R112 in every market (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the headlights follow the ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested: headlight beam pattern conforms to ECE R112 requirements as requested by customers (subject to certification in each market).
assumptions: Market-specific approval and adjustments may be necessary to reconcile differing market regulations.
uncertainties: Some markets have different headlamp regulations that may conflict; harmonization may not be fully possible.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation request — market approvals and certification are out of scope for product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Volume knob magnetic encoder specification (component-level request)
drafts.description: Customers requested the volume knob use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component: volume knob to use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder as specified by the customer signal.
assumptions: This is a component-level engineering specification to be assessed by hardware/UX teams for feasibility and integration.
uncertainties: Final decision depends on supplier availability, EMI constraints and integration with HMI software.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/component-level specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirement set.

drafts.title: Side window glass thickness specification (component-level request)
drafts.description: Customers requested side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component-level spec: side windows to be 4.5 mm laminated glass as stated by the customer signal.
assumptions: Glass thickness and lamination choices are engineering decisions that impact weight, NVH and safety.
uncertainties: Trade-offs with glazing weight, acoustic performance and regulatory requirements may alter final spec.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/component-level specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirement set.

drafts.title: Seat foam density specification (component-level request)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat cushion foam with a density of 55 kg/m³.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component-level spec: seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ as stated by the customer signal.
assumptions: Foam density selection affects long-term comfort, weight and durability and will be validated in durability testing.
uncertainties: Final density may be adjusted for durability, weight or supply constraints.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/component-level specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirement set.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business/financial ask)
drafts.description: Customers request that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested guarantee: residual value of 60% after five years as stated by the customer signal.
assumptions: Residual value guarantees are a commercial/financial product decision requiring legal and finance evaluation.
uncertainties: Market fluctuations, mileage and condition clauses will affect any guarantee; feasibility depends on business case.
drafts.scope_reason: Business case/financial guarantee — pricing and residual-value guarantees are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Production cost reduction request (business target)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW cut production cost per car by 8%.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested target: reduce production cost per car by 8% as stated by the customer signal.
assumptions: Production cost targets are corporate/operations objectives that must be validated by manufacturing and procurement teams.
uncertainties: Cost-saving measures may impact perceived quality or features; trade-offs need cross-functional review.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/production cost target — out of scope for customer-facing product requirement drafting.
